resources.title: Data Pipeline Explained: The Warehouse Analogy
resources.description: A one-page diagram walking the full modern data pipeline — object storage as the loading dock, Spark/Databricks as the processing area, a warehouse as the organized storage shelves, and Power BI/SQL as the analysts querying it — with a glossary of bucket, object, folder, stage, and table.

resources.title: Databricks Medallion Architecture
resources.description: Bronze/Silver/Gold layer reference diagram showing what each layer holds, who uses it, and why the medallion pattern exists — data quality, auditability, reusability, scalability, and governance.

resources.title: The Amazon Fulfillment Center Analogy for Spark
resources.description: A full-page reference on how Spark actually executes a job — clusters, executors, partitions, the DAG, narrow vs. wide transformations, joins (shuffle vs. broadcast), caching, repartition vs. coalesce, actions, and reading the Spark UI.

resources.title: Why Object Storage Still Matters After Data Is in the Warehouse
resources.description: Explains why raw files stay in cheap object storage even after they've been loaded into a warehouse — reprocessing, audit/compliance, lineage, replay for new systems, and cost — with the full pipeline shown end to end.

resources.title: Lakehouse Architecture & Building a Production Data Pipeline Infographic
resources.description: A two-part reference: the lakehouse concept itself (combining a data lake's flexibility with a data warehouse's performance), the Databricks platform (notebooks, jobs, SQL, clusters, Unity Catalog), Delta Lake's core features (ACID transactions, time travel, schema evolution, high performance), and the medallion Bronze/Silver/Gold architecture — paired with a full production-pipeline walkthrough (ingest, orchestrate, transform, store, analyze/AI, deliver) using a real retail sales pipeline example, the end-to-end data flow from sources through the lakehouse to consumers, and the key skills the whole thing builds.
